scope: abstract protocol and operational-activation semantics; no cryptographic implementation

B1.name: Triple-KEM/PQNoise-style SDLS key update
source_supported_semantics: the construction is a standalone key exchange that outputs fresh SDLS keys
final keys are derived only after the handshake is complete for the party in question
missing or out-of-order required fragments cause abort/drop unless a lower layer repairs ordering or loss

default_confirm_loss.meaning: initiator completion is ambiguous to the responder; neither endpoint changes the active SDLS epoch

non_attribution: The deferred activation policy is an experimental SDLS integration rule, not a claim about the Triple-KEM paper.
The paper does not specify an operational SDLS commit or rollback procedure.
Final-confirmation loss is not labeled a permanent lockout without an explicit activation policy.

B2.name: Poettering-Roesler URKE-inspired strict evolution baseline
B2.construction_family: unidirectional ratcheted key exchange using generic KEM encapsulation and evolving endpoint state
selection_rationale: matches the study's ground-compromise threat direction
uses a generic KEM abstraction rather than requiring the more complex bidirectional HIBE-like construction
introduces fresh entropy and evolves state after each send or receipt
provides a clean strict-state baseline for measuring synchronization loss

strict_model_decisions.sender_transition: ground derives the new session state and deletes the prior sender state when the update is sent
strict_model_decisions.receiver_transition: spacecraft derives and installs the matching state only after accepting the update ciphertext
strict_model_decisions.status_telemetry: evidence of completion, not a ratchet transition

non_attribution: This is a TT&C operational adaptation of the URKE state-evolution pattern, not a claim of protocol conformance.
The simulator does not implement the paper's cryptographic algorithms or proof model.
The strict deletion policy is deliberately recovery-hostile and serves as the comparison baseline for T1.

requirements_before_T1: B1 source and integration semantics encoded in tests
B2 construction family and role mapping encoded in tests
baseline fault outcomes stable under deterministic replay
independent cryptography review of the semantic mapping
